photochemical-smog-s2.title: Afternoon ozone at one monitor on four July days

table.caption: Highest one-hour ozone and the weather at a city monitor (invented data for practice)

items.q: At about what time does ozone reach its highest level on this day?
options: About 8 a.m., at 95 ppb
About 2 p.m., at 120 ppb
About 9 a.m., at 85 ppb
About 6 p.m., at 60 ppb

why.correct: The dashed ozone line peaks at 120 ppb at hour 14, which is 2 p.m., six hours after the NO peak.
options: That is the NO peak during the morning commute; ozone is still low then.
Right: the ozone line is highest at hour 14.
That is the NO2 peak. Ozone builds later, as sunlight strengthens.
At 6 p.m. ozone is falling; its peak came four hours earlier.

items.q: Why does the NO2 peak come about an hour after the NO peak?
options: NO from morning traffic reacts in the air to form NO2
Cars switch from releasing NO to NO2 as their engines warm
NO2 forms when sunlight splits ozone apart in the afternoon
NO2 drifts in from a coal plant far upwind of the city

why.correct: Cars release mostly NO. In the air, NO reacts to form NO2, so NO2 builds up just after the NO from the morning rush.
options: Right: NO2 is made from the NO, so it peaks after it.
Engines release mostly NO all day; NO2 forms in the air.
Sunlight splits NO2 to help make ozone, not the other way round, and the NO2 peak is in the morning.
The NO2 rise follows the local NO rise from traffic, not a distant source.

items.q: Between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m., NO2 falls from 85 to 35 ppb while ozone rises from 35 to 120 ppb. Which process explains both changes?
options: Ozone sinks down from the stratosphere at midday
Wind blows the NO2 away and brings ozone from the sea
Rain washes NO2 out and leaves ozone behind in the air
Sunlight splits NO2 and the oxygen atom forms ozone

why.correct: Sunlight splits NO2 into NO and a single oxygen atom. The oxygen atom joins an O2 molecule to make O3. So NO2 is used up as ozone is made.
options: The ozone layer stays far above; this ozone forms near the ground from NO2.
Wind does not explain why the two change in step with the sunlight.
The day is sunny; nothing in the graph points to rain.
Right: NO2 is used up as O3 is made, which is why one falls as the other rises.

items.q: Find the percent change in ozone from 6 a.m. to 2 p.m.

why.correct: $\frac{(120\,\text{ppb} - 10\,\text{ppb})}{10\,\text{ppb}} \times 100 = 1{,}100\%$. Ozone was 12 times its 6 a.m. level.

mistakes.why: You divided by the 2 p.m. value. Percent change divides by the old (6 a.m.) value, 10 ppb.
1,200% is the new value as a percent of the old. Percent change subtracts first: (120 - 10) / 10 × 100.
11 is the fraction. Multiply by 100 for a percent: 1,100%.

items.q: Which comparison in the table best shows that sunlight drives ozone formation?
options: Monday was the hottest day and also had the most ozone
Thursday was the coolest day and had the least ozone
Overcast Wednesday had half the ozone of clear Tuesday
Tuesday was cooler than Monday and had less ozone

why.correct: Wednesday and Tuesday differ mostly in the sky: overcast Wednesday at 29 °C had 48 ppb, clear Tuesday at 31 °C had 96 ppb. Less sunlight, far less ozone.
options: Heat and sun both rise on Monday, so this alone cannot separate sunlight from temperature.
Thursday did not have the least ozone; overcast Wednesday did.
Right: similar temperatures, but the cloudy day made far less ozone.
Both days were clear, so this compares temperature, not sunlight.

items.q: Find the percent change in the highest ozone from Monday to Wednesday.

mistakes.why: You divided by Wednesday's value. Divide by the old (Monday) value, 118 ppb.
Ozone fell, so the change is negative: about -59.3%.

items.q: The city issues ozone alerts asking people with asthma to stay indoors. On which kind of day is an alert most likely?
options: A cold, overcast morning in winter
A hot, clear afternoon in summer
A rainy evening after the rush hour
A windy night just before dawn

why.correct: Ozone forms fastest with strong sunlight and heat, so hot, clear afternoons, like Monday, bring the highest levels.
options: Little sunlight and cold air slow ozone formation.
Right: strong sunlight and heat make ozone fastest.
Without sunlight, ozone falls in the evening.
At night there is no sunlight to split NO2, so ozone is low.

items.q: What two kinds of primary pollutant react in sunlight to form photochemical smog?
options: Nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds
Sulfur dioxide and carbon dioxide from coal
Carbon monoxide and lead from old car engines
Methane and water vapor released from swamps and wetlands

why.correct: Nitrogen oxides from hot combustion and volatile organic compounds from fuel vapor and solvents react in sunlight to make ozone and other smog chemicals.
options: Right: NOx and VOCs plus sunlight make photochemical smog.
SO2 and soot make the gray, sooty kind of smog; CO2 is not a smog ingredient.
Neither is a key ingredient of photochemical smog.
Neither drives the sunlight reactions that make smog ozone.

items.q: How does the presence of VOCs let ozone build up near the ground during the day?
options: VOCs split in sunlight into ozone molecules directly
VOCs cool the air so the ozone sinks down to the ground
VOCs block sunlight so ozone is not broken apart
VOCs react with NO, so NO no longer breaks ozone down

why.correct: Without VOCs, NO reacts with ozone and breaks it back down. VOCs react with the NO instead, forming photochemical oxidants, so ozone is not used up and accumulates.
options: VOCs do not break into ozone; ozone forms from an oxygen atom freed from NO2.
VOCs do not cool the air; the effect is chemical.
VOCs are gases that do not block sunlight; smog forms in strong sun.
Right: the NO that would destroy ozone is tied up by VOC reactions.

items.q: Ozone in a city usually drops after sunset. Why?
options: Ozone rises at night to rejoin the ozone layer
Cooler night air turns ozone into sulfur dioxide
No new ozone forms, and NO uses up what is there
Trees take in ozone at night through their roots

why.correct: Sunlight is needed to split NO2 and make ozone. After dark no new ozone forms, and NO from evening traffic reacts with the ozone that is there, using it up.
options: Ozone near the ground does not drift up to the stratosphere overnight.
Ozone does not turn into SO2; they are different elements.
Right: no sunlight means no new ozone, and NO destroys the rest.
Trees do not absorb ozone through their roots.

items.q: Ozone in the stratosphere protects life, but ozone near the ground is a pollutant. What is the difference?
options: They are two different molecules with the same name
Up high it absorbs UV; down low people breathe it in
Ozone near the ground is harmless at any level
Ozone up high comes from car exhaust drifting upward

why.correct: Same molecule, different place. High in the stratosphere O3 absorbs UV radiation; in the air we breathe it irritates and damages lung tissue and plant leaves.
options: Both are O3; only the location differs.
Right: location decides whether ozone helps or harms.
Ozone near the ground irritates lungs and harms crops.
Stratospheric ozone forms from O2 split by UV light, not from exhaust.

items.q: Which group of people is most at risk on a day with high photochemical smog?
options: Children with asthma playing outdoors
Office workers in sealed, filtered buildings
People in rural areas far upwind of the city
People who are sleeping indoors at night

why.correct: Ozone irritates the airways and makes them swell, so people with asthma or other lung disease, children and people exercising hard outdoors are hurt most.
options: Right: active lungs take in more ozone, and asthma makes airways sensitive.
Indoor air in sealed, filtered buildings has much less ozone.
Smog builds in and downwind of the city, not far upwind.
Ozone peaks in the afternoon, and less is indoors.

items.q: Two cities have the same traffic. City X is sunny and warm most of the year; city Y is cool and often cloudy. Which will have more photochemical smog, and why?
options: City Y, because clouds trap the pollutants near the ground
Neither, because smog depends on traffic alone
City Y, because cool air holds more ozone than warm air
City X, because sunlight and warmth drive the reactions

why.correct: Photochemical smog needs sunlight to split NO2, and warmth speeds the reactions, so the same NOx and VOCs make more smog in sunny, warm city X.
options: Clouds cut the sunlight that smog needs; they do not add ozone.
Traffic supplies the NOx and VOCs, but sunlight is needed to react them.
Cool, cloudy weather slows ozone formation.
Right: sun and heat speed every step that makes ozone.

items.q: Put the steps that form photochemical smog on a sunny day in order.
options: Morning traffic releases NO and VOCs
NO reacts in the air to form NO2
Sunlight splits NO2 into NO and an oxygen atom
The oxygen atom joins O2 to form ozone
VOCs tie up NO, so ozone builds through the afternoon

why.correct: Emission, then NO to NO2, then sunlight splitting NO2, then O + O2 forming O3, and VOCs keep the ozone from being destroyed.

items.q: A city's highest ozone readings averaged 96 ppb before a rule cut VOCs from paints and fuel, and 72 ppb after. Write the setup for the percent change, then the answer.

why.correct: $\frac{(72 - 96)}{96} \times 100 = -25\%$: the rule went with a 25% fall in peak ozone.

mistakes.why: Divide by the old value, 96 ppb, not the new one.
Without brackets the division happens first. Write (72 - 96) / 96 × 100.
Subtract old from new: (72 - 96). Ozone fell, so the change is negative.
Ozone fell, so the percent change is negative: -25%.

items.q: Propose a city-level solution, other than a rule on paints, that would reduce photochemical smog, and say how it works.

why.correct: Fewer car trips mean less NO and VOCs, the two ingredients sunlight turns into ozone. It fits a city and respects the "other than paints" limit.

specific.frame: The city could ___, which reduces ___, so less ozone forms in sunlight.

action.label: Solution
options: expand bus and light-rail service so fewer people drive to work
limit the solvents allowed in house paints
plant more trees that release VOCs

why.1: The question says other than a rule on paints.
why.2: Trees that release VOCs would add an ingredient of smog, not remove one.

what.label: What it reduces
options: the CO2 that traps heat
the NOx and VOCs from car exhaust
the sulfur dioxide from coal plants

why.0: CO2 is not an ingredient of photochemical smog.
why.2: SO2 is not the driver of photochemical smog; NOx and VOCs are.

specific.model: The city could expand bus and light-rail service so fewer people drive, which reduces the NOx and VOCs from car exhaust, so less ozone forms in sunlight.
